findings.text: IPv4 protocol identifiers use fixed values: IPPROTO_IP 0, ICMP 1, IGMP 2, IPIP 4, TCP 6, EGP 8, PUP 12, UDP 17, IDP 22, TP 29, DCCP 33, IPV6 41, RSVP 46, GRE 47, ESP 50, AH 51, MTP 92, BEETPH 94, ENCAP 98, PIM 103, COMP 108, L2TP 115, SCTP 132, UDPLITE 136, MPLS 137, ETHERNET 143, AGGFRAG 144, RAW 255, SMC 256, MPTCP 262, followed by a MAX sentinel. Each name is also available as a self alias.
The IPv4 address holder is a structure with a single 32 bit network order member for the address and no other members or variants.

IPv4 socket options 1 to 19 are IP_TOS 1, IP_TTL 2, IP_HDRINCL 3, IP_OPTIONS 4, IP_ROUTER_ALERT 5, IP_RECVOPTS 6, IP_RETOPTS 7, IP_PKTINFO 8, IP_PKTOPTIONS 9, IP_MTU_DISCOVER 10, IP_RECVERR 11, IP_RECVTTL 12, IP_RECVTOS 13, IP_MTU 14, IP_FREEBIND 15, IP_IPSEC_POLICY 16, IP_XFRM_POLICY 17, IP_PASSSEC 18, IP_TRANSPARENT 19.

Further IPv4 options are IP_ORIGDSTADDR 20 with IP_RECVORIGDSTADDR equal to it, IP_MINTTL 21, IP_NODEFRAG 22, IP_CHECKSUM 23, IP_BIND_ADDRESS_NO_PORT 24, IP_RECVFRAGSIZE 25, IP_RECVERR_RFC4884 26. IP_RECVRETOPTS equals IP_RETOPTS.

Path MTU discovery modes share values in both families: DONT 0, WANT 1, DO 2, PROBE 3, INTERFACE 4, OMIT 5. The IPv4 names are IP_PMTUDISC_DONT through IP_PMTUDISC_OMIT and the IPv6 names are IPV6_PMTUDISC_DONT through IPV6_PMTUDISC_OMIT with the same numbers.

Multicast and related IPv4 options are IP_MULTICAST_IF 32, IP_MULTICAST_TTL 33, IP_MULTICAST_LOOP 34, IP_ADD_MEMBERSHIP 35, IP_DROP_MEMBERSHIP 36, IP_UNBLOCK_SOURCE 37, IP_BLOCK_SOURCE 38, IP_ADD_SOURCE_MEMBERSHIP 39, IP_DROP_SOURCE_MEMBERSHIP 40, IP_MSFILTER 41, MCAST_JOIN_GROUP 42, MCAST_BLOCK_SOURCE 43, MCAST_UNBLOCK_SOURCE 44, MCAST_LEAVE_GROUP 45, MCAST_JOIN_SOURCE_GROUP 46, MCAST_LEAVE_SOURCE_GROUP 47, MCAST_MSFILTER 48, IP_MULTICAST_ALL 49, IP_UNICAST_IF 50, IP_LOCAL_PORT_RANGE 51, IP_PROTOCOL 52. Modes are MCAST_EXCLUDE 0 and MCAST_INCLUDE 1. Defaults IP_DEFAULT_MULTICAST_TTL and IP_DEFAULT_MULTICAST_LOOP are both 1.

Membership management uses related layouts. The basic request pairs a group address with an interface address. The indexed variant carries group, local address, and a signed interface index. The source specific variant stores three raw network order words for group, interface, and source. The source filter variant stores group, interface, filter mode, and source count followed by a trailing source list visible both as a one element array and as a flexible array. Protocol independent requests store an interface index plus generic socket storage for group, optionally plus storage for source. The generic filter overlays two equivalent views with auxiliary suffixed versus plain names, each with interface, group, mode, count, and trailing source storage.

Variable length filter sizes are computed as base structure size minus the placeholder trailing element plus the requested count times one element size. One helper applies this with 32 bit entries and the other with generic socket storage entries.

Packet information carries an interface index plus two IPv4 addresses for the specified destination and the packet address. The IPv4 socket address carries a kernel family, a network order port, an IPv4 address, and trailing pad extending the total to 16 bytes. The size constant is 16 and the pad is also known under a BSD compatibility alias.

Classful tests inspect high bits of a host order value: class A clears the top bit, B matches 10, C matches 110, D and multicast match 1110, E matches 1111, loopback has 127 in the top octet, bad class and experimental equal all ones. Masks and shifts are A FF000000 shift 24 max 128, B FFFF0000 shift 16 max 65536, C FFFFFF00 shift 8, D E0000000, E FFFFFFFF shift 0. Host portions are the complement of the net masks.

Special IPv4 values are INADDR_ANY zero, INADDR_BROADCAST all ones, INADDR_NONE all ones, INADDR_DUMMY C0000008 hex, IN_LOOPBACKNET 127, INADDR_LOOPBACK 7F000001 hex, INADDR_UNSPEC_GROUP E0000000, INADDR_ALLHOSTS_GROUP E0000001, INADDR_ALLRTRS_GROUP E0000002, INADDR_ALLSNOOPERS_GROUP E000006A, INADDR_MAX_LOCAL_GROUP E00000FF.

IPv6 addressing uses a 16 byte union always visible as bytes and optionally as network order 16 bit or 32 bit arrays with short aliases for each view. The IPv6 socket address carries family, network order port, flow information, address, and scope identifier. Multicast membership pairs a group address with an interface index and has an alias equating an alternate address name to the group. Flow label requests carry destination, label, action, share, flags, expiry, linger, and pad plus trailing packet option bytes.

Flow label control uses IPV6_FL_A_GET 0, A_PUT 1, A_RENEW 2, flags F_CREATE 1, F_EXCL 2, F_REFLECT 4, F_REMOTE 8, sharing S_NONE 0, S_EXCL 1, S_PROCESS 2, S_USER 3, S_ANY 255. Masks are IPV6_FLOWINFO_FLOWLABEL 000FFFFF hex and IPV6_FLOWINFO_PRIORITY 0FF00000 hex. Priorities step by 0100 hex from UNCHARACTERIZED 0000, FILLER, UNATTENDED, RESERVED1, BULK, RESERVED2, INTERACTIVE, CONTROL, then 8 through 15 ending at 0F00.

IPv6 header identifiers are IPPROTO_HOPOPTS 0, ROUTING 43, FRAGMENT 44, ICMPV6 58, NONE 59, DSTOPTS 60, MH 135. Option TLV types are IPV6_TLV_PAD1 0, PADN 1, ROUTERALERT 5, CALIPSO 7, IOAM 49, JUMBO 194, HAO 201.

Lower IPv6 options are IPV6_ADDRFORM 1, 2292PKTINFO 2, 2292HOPOPTS 3, 2292DSTOPTS 4, 2292RTHDR 5, 2292PKTOPTIONS 6, CHECKSUM 7, 2292HOPLIMIT 8, NEXTHOP 9, AUTHHDR 10 obsolete, FLOWINFO 11, UNICAST_HOPS 16, MULTICAST_IF 17, MULTICAST_HOPS 18, MULTICAST_LOOP 19, ADD_MEMBERSHIP 20, DROP_MEMBERSHIP 21, ROUTER_ALERT 22, MTU_DISCOVER 23, MTU 24, RECVERR 25, V6ONLY 26, JOIN_ANYCAST 27, LEAVE_ANYCAST 28, MULTICAST_ALL 29, ROUTER_ALERT_ISOLATE 30, RECVERR_RFC4884 31, FLOWLABEL_MGR 32, FLOWINFO_SEND 33, IPSEC_POLICY 34, XFRM_POLICY 35, HDRINCL 36.

Upper IPv6 options are RECVPKTINFO 49, PKTINFO 50, RECVHOPLIMIT 51, HOPLIMIT 52, RECVHOPOPTS 53, HOPOPTS 54, RTHDRDSTOPTS 55, RECVRTHDR 56, RTHDR 57, RECVDSTOPTS 58, DSTOPTS 59, RECVPATHMTU 60, PATHMTU 61, DONTFRAG 62, RECVTCLASS 66, TCLASS 67, AUTOFLOWLABEL 70, ADDR_PREFERENCES 72, MINHOPCOUNT 73, ORIGDSTADDR 74 with RECVORIGDSTADDR equal to it, TRANSPARENT 75, UNICAST_IF 76, RECVFRAGSIZE 77, FREEBIND 78. Preference flags are TMP 0001, PUBLIC 0002, COA 0004, CGA 0008, PUBTMP_DEFAULT 0100, HOME 0400, NONCGA 0800 hex.

Diagnostics identify a socket by network order ports, source and destination addresses as four network order words, interface index, and a two word cookie with an all ones no cookie value. Requests carry family, lengths or protocol, extension mask, pad, state mask, optional table mask, and the socket identifier. A raw variant adds a raw protocol octet.

Diagnostic commands are TCPDIAG_GETSOCK 18 and DCCPDIAG_GETSOCK 19 with INET_DIAG_GETSOCK_MAX 24. Request attributes in order from zero are NONE, BYTECODE, SK_BPF_STORAGES, PROTOCOL, with INET_DIAG_REQ_MAX one less than the internal sentinel.

Bytecode filtering is a jump machine where each operation carries an opcode plus yes and no offsets. Opcodes in order from zero cover no operation, jump, source and destination port ordered and equality tests, automatic handling, source and destination address tests, device, mark, and cgroup tests. Address tests carry family, prefix length, port, and trailing address bytes. Mark tests carry value and mask.

Replies report family, state, timer kind, retransmit count, socket identifier, expiry, queue lengths, user, and inode. Timer kinds in order from zero are off, on, keepalive, timewait, zero probe, and delayed ack. Memory accounting carries four counters for read, write, forward, and true size. Socket option reporting packs one bit flags for error queue, internal kind, free bind, header inclusion, multicast loop and all, transparency, no fragment, no port binding, RFC4884 errors, and deferred connect plus spares. Vegas reporting carries enabled, round trip count, round trip time, and minimum round trip.

Diagnostic extensions in order from zero are NONE, MEMINFO, INFO, VEGASINFO, CONG, TOS, TCLASS, SKMEMINFO, SHUTDOWN, DCTCPINFO, PROTOCOL, SKV6ONLY, LOCALS, PEERS, PAD, MARK, BBRINFO, CLASS_ID, MD5SIG, ULP_INFO, SK_BPF_STORAGES, CGROUP_ID, SOCKOPT, with INET_DIAG_MAX one less than the sentinel. Upper layer kinds are UNSPEC, NAME, TLS, MPTCP with a similarly derived maximum. Later extensions reuse earlier request bits, protocol is response only, and mark needs elevated privilege.

These headers export the stable user to kernel contract for IPv4 and IPv6 addresses, socket addresses, multicast and source management, socket controls, flow label handling, and socket diagnostics over netlink with bytecode filtering.

Trailing one element and flexible arrays must be sized with the provided helpers rather than base size alone or source lists truncate or overrun. Unions expose the same bytes under alternate names so a write through one alias is visible through the other. Bytecode offsets and variable address tails need bounds checks to avoid overread.

Several names are aliases and must compare equal: receive return options equals return options, receive original destination equals original destination in both families, pad equals the BSD zero name, alternate access address equals group address, multicast test equals class D test, experimental test equals bad class test, and short s6 names equal the corresponding union members. Total IPv4 socket address size stays 16.
